lessonTitle: Phase Change and Property Tables: Quality and Superheated Steam

blocks.text: A pressure cooker holds liquid water and steam together at a pressure well above atmospheric. At one fixed pressure the temperature of the mixture is also fixed, so pressure and temperature cannot tell you how much of the water has boiled. You need one more property, and the steam tables are how engineers look it up.

blocks.markdown: A pure substance such as water exists as compressed liquid, saturated mixture or superheated vapour depending on its state. On a **$T$-$v$ diagram** the **saturation dome** is a bell-shaped curve; the left branch is the **saturated liquid line** (specific volume $v_f$) and the right branch is the **saturated vapour line** (specific volume $v_g$). Inside the dome liquid and vapour coexist at the saturation temperature $T_{sat}(p)$, and outside it the fluid is a single phase.

rows: Saturated liquid table (approximation) or compressed liquid table
blocks.caption: Locating a state relative to the saturation dome

blocks.title: Quality
blocks.text: Quality $x$ is the mass fraction of vapour in a saturated mixture, $x=m_g/(m_f+m_g)$, dimensionless between 0 (saturated liquid) and 1 (saturated vapour). It is defined only inside the dome. Any specific property of the mixture is a mass-weighted average.

blocks.caption: The subscript fg means (value for vapour minus value for liquid); the same form works for u, h and s

blocks.title: Quality from specific volume
blocks.prompt: A rigid vessel contains a saturated water mixture at 200 kPa with specific volume v = 0.30 m$^3$/kg. At 200 kPa, vf = 0.001061 and vg = 0.88578 m$^3$/kg (approximate table values). Find the quality.

steps.text: Check the region: $v_f<0.30<v_g$, so it is a mixture.

blocks.answer: x = 0.338, so about 34 % of the mass is vapour even though the vapour occupies almost all the volume.

blocks.markdown: When the state is **superheated** you read the table at the given pressure for the temperature rows. If the temperature falls between two rows, use **linear interpolation**. For a property $y$ and temperature $T$ between $T_a$ and $T_b$:

blocks.caption: Interpolate each property separately; keep the pressure fixed

blocks.title: Interpolating superheated steam
blocks.prompt: Steam at 1 MPa and 280 C. The superheated table at 1 MPa gives (approximate values) at 250 C: h = 2942.6 kJ/kg, s = 6.9265 kJ/(kg K); at 300 C: h = 3051.2 kJ/kg, s = 7.1246 kJ/(kg K). Find h and s at 280 C.
blocks.answer: h is about 3007.8 kJ/kg and s is about 7.045 kJ/(kg K). The temperature 280 C exceeds Tsat of 179.9 C at 1 MPa, confirming superheat.

blocks.title: Locating a state on the T-v diagram
blocks.prompt: Water at 150 C has specific volume 0.50 m$^3$/kg. At 150 C the saturation values are vf = 0.001091 and vg = 0.39248 m$^3$/kg (approximate). Where is the state?

steps.text: The state lies to the right of the saturated vapour line at the same temperature, so it is superheated vapour at a pressure below the saturation pressure of 150 C.

blocks.answer: The state is superheated vapour: use the superheated table with the pressure found by matching T and v.

blocks.markdown: In a rigid closed vessel heating at constant volume follows a vertical line on a $v$-$p$ or $T$-$v$ diagram (constant $v$). If the average $v$ is smaller than the critical specific volume the vessel ends up filled with liquid, and if larger, with vapour. This is why the volume-based quality is not the same as the quality by mass.

blocks.title: Volume fraction is not quality
blocks.text: A vessel that is 50 % vapour by volume at 100 kPa is almost entirely liquid by mass, because vapour is roughly 1600 times less dense. Never equate volume fraction with quality.

blocks.title: Order of attack
blocks.text: Find the saturation values at the stated pressure or temperature first. Compare v (or T) to decide the region, and then use the matching table or formula.

points: Compressed liquid, saturated mixture and superheated vapour are distinguished by comparing T with Tsat or v with vf and vg.
Quality x = (v - vf)/(vg - vf) is the mass fraction of vapour in a saturated mixture; h and s follow the same pattern.
For superheated steam, interpolate linearly between the table rows at the given pressure.
Volume fraction of vapour differs hugely from the mass fraction (quality).

questions.stem: Water at a given pressure has a specific volume less than the saturated liquid value vf. What is its state?

distractorRationale.a: A mixture lies between vf and vg.
distractorRationale.c: Vapour has v greater than vg.

questions.explanation: At a fixed pressure or temperature, vf is the smallest specific volume in the dome. A smaller value means the liquid is colder than saturation, so it is compressed liquid.

questions.stem: What does the quality x of a saturated mixture measure?

options.text: The mass of vapour divided by the total mass

questions.correctOptionText: The mass of vapour divided by the total mass
questions.explanation: Quality is the vapour mass fraction, x = m_g/(m_f + m_g). It equals 0 for saturated liquid and 1 for saturated vapour.

questions.stem: Water at 100 kPa has a temperature of 90 C. The saturation temperature at 100 kPa is about 99.6 C. What is the state?

distractorRationale.b: T is below Tsat, not above.
distractorRationale.c: A mixture would be at 99.6 C.

questions.explanation: At a given pressure, a temperature below Tsat means the water has not reached the boiling point, so it is liquid. Since it is not at saturation, it is compressed (subcooled) liquid.

questions.stem: Steam at 2 MPa is at 340 C. The superheated table gives h at 300 C and 350 C. Which expression gives the interpolated enthalpy?

distractorRationale.b: This assumes the midpoint, which is 325 C.
distractorRationale.c: This is the difference, not an interpolated value.

questions.explanation: Linear interpolation moves from the lower row by the fraction of the temperature interval traversed. Here 40/50 = 0.8 of the difference is added to h300.

questions.stem: A closed vessel at 100 kPa contains a saturated mixture whose vapour fills half of the volume. With vf = 0.001043 and vg = 1.694 m$^3$/kg, what is the quality?

distractorRationale.a: This confuses volume fraction with mass fraction.
distractorRationale.d: Vapour is far less dense than liquid, so the quality is not near 1.

questions.explanation: Half the volume of liquid has a mass proportional to 0.5/0.001043 and half the volume of vapour has a mass proportional to 0.5/1.694. The vapour mass fraction is therefore 0.0006, which is tiny.

questions.stem: At 500 kPa a saturated mixture has v = 0.10 m$^3$/kg. At 500 kPa the table gives vf = 0.001093 and vg = 0.37483 m$^3$/kg (approximate values). Find the quality (dimensionless).
questions.explanation: The quality is x = (v - vf)/(vg - vf) = (0.10 - 0.001093)/(0.37483 - 0.001093) = 0.2646. The state lies inside the dome because vf < v < vg.

questions.stem: At 1 MPa the superheated table gives h = 3051.2 kJ/kg at 300 C and h = 3157.7 kJ/kg at 350 C (approximate values). Find h at 330 C by linear interpolation, in kJ/kg.
questions.explanation: The interpolation fraction is (330 - 300)/(350 - 300) = 0.6, so h = 3051.2 + 0.6 x (3157.7 - 3051.2) = 3115.1 kJ/kg. The pressure is held constant in this method.

questions.stem: A rigid 0.60 m$^3$ vessel holds 3.0 kg of a saturated water mixture at 150 kPa, where vf = 0.001053 and vg = 1.1594 m$^3$/kg (approximate table values). Find the mass of vapour in kg.
Sketch the saturation dome on a T-v diagram and describe where compressed liquid, saturated mixture and superheated vapour lie. How can you tell from given T and p which region a state is in?
markingGuide: Dome bounded by saturated liquid line (vf) on the left and saturated vapour line (vg) on the right, topped by the critical point
Compressed liquid is to the left of the dome, with v < vf
Mixture is inside the dome, vf < v < vg
Superheated vapour is to the right and above, v > vg
From T and p: T < Tsat(p) means compressed liquid, T = Tsat means mixture or saturated, T > Tsat(p) means superheated
questions.explanation: Specific volume increases from left to right, so liquid is on the left and vapour on the right. A temperature comparison with Tsat at the given pressure also places the state, with T above Tsat meaning superheated.

questions.stem: Describe the steps to find (a) the quality of a saturated mixture from its specific volume, and (b) the enthalpy of superheated steam at a temperature between two table rows. State what must be checked before applying each.
markingGuide: (a) Read vf and vg at the given pressure or temperature
Check vf < v < vg before using the formula
(b) Check T > Tsat at the pressure
Take the two rows at the same pressure that bracket T and interpolate h = ha + (T - Ta)/(Tb - Ta)(hb - ha)
Entropy handled the same way, property by property
questions.explanation: Both procedures begin by placing the state in the correct region so that the correct table and formula are used. Linear interpolation is acceptable because properties vary smoothly over small temperature intervals.
